2188def _on_data_source_pick() -> None: 

2189 """Route the main-view picker's choice through the pre-widget seam (UX-25). 

2190 

2191 An ``on_change`` callback: it runs before the rerun's script body, so 

2192 ``render_sidebar_data_source`` — which pops ``_pending_source_choice`` at the 

2193 top of ``main`` — applies the new source on the *same* run that renders it. 

2194 The picker rides its own widget key (``data_source_picker``) rather than 

2195 writing ``data_source_choice`` directly, so a deep link / saved config can 

2196 keep assigning the canonical key without the widget reconciling it away. 

2197 """ 

2198 picked = st.session_state.get("data_source_picker") 

2199 if picked: 

2200 st.session_state["_pending_source_choice"] = picked 

2201 

2202 

2203def render_data_source_picker(host=None) -> None: 

2204 """Render the data-source picker in the main view (UX-25). 

2205 

2206 Sits on the "Filter by" row, left of the label, so the top of the page reads 

2207 left-to-right as *which dataset → how to narrow it → which trial* — the app is 

2208 built to be used with the sidebar closed. Renders from the entry list 

2209 :func:`render_sidebar_data_source` published earlier this run; a pick is 

2210 applied on the next run via :func:`_on_data_source_pick`. 

2211 

2212 The compact row holds the selectbox only; managing sources (➕ Add data, 

2213 removing an uploaded dataset, contributing a corpus) lives behind the ➕ 

2214 popover beside it. 

2215 """ 

2216 # Imported lazily (not at module top) to avoid the app⇄wizard import cycle. 

2217 from scanpath_studio.wizard import _enter_add_data_wizard, _remove_dataset 

2218 

2219 entries = list(st.session_state.get("_data_source_entries") or []) 

2220 if not entries: 

2221 return 

2222 kinds: Dict[str, str] = dict(st.session_state.get("_data_source_kinds") or {}) 

2223 uploaded = list(st.session_state.get("_data_source_uploaded") or []) 

2224 

2225 def _entry_label(token: str) -> str: 

2226 tag = kinds.get(token, "") 

2227 if token in PUBLIC_DATASET_REGISTRY: 

2228 name = _public_dataset_label(token) 

2229 elif token in uploaded: 

2230 name = f"{token} (yours)" 

2231 else: 

2232 name = token 

2233 return f"{tag} {name}".strip() 

2234 

2235 # Keyed wrapper → stable `.st-key-…` selector for the spotlight tour. 

2236 box = (host if host is not None else st).container(key="tour_grp_data_source") 

2237 pick_col, add_col = box.columns([5.6, 1], vertical_alignment="center") 

2238 # Mirror the canonical key onto the widget key before it instantiates, so a 

2239 # deep link / restore / wizard finalize shows up in the picker. 

2240 current = st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") 

2241 if current in entries: 

2242 st.session_state["data_source_picker"] = current 

2243 pick_col.selectbox( 

2244 "Data source", 

2245 entries, 

2246 format_func=_entry_label, 

2247 help=data_dictionary_help_text(), 

2248 key="data_source_picker", 

2249 on_change=_on_data_source_pick, 

2250 label_visibility="collapsed", 

2251 ) 

2252 # UX-47: `railbtn_*`, like every other trigger on the four control rows above 

2253 # the plot. It was the one that never joined UX-27's shared shape, and it 

2254 # showed: a 40 px-tall stretched rectangle beside 27 px pills, which also made 

2255 # this row the tallest of the four for no reason. 

2256 manage = add_col.container(key="railbtn_data_add").popover( 

2257 "➕", width="content", help="Add or remove datasets." 

2258 ) 

2259 # The state change runs in an on_click callback (before widgets instantiate) 

2260 # so it can reassign the data_source_choice key — see _enter_add_data_wizard. 

2261 # The callback fires, then Streamlit reruns into the wizard branch. 

2262 manage.button( 

2263 "➕ Add data", 

2264 key="add_data_btn", 

2265 on_click=_enter_add_data_wizard, 

2266 help="Upload your own eye-tracking tables.", 

2267 width="stretch", 

2268 ) 

2269 # Let the user remove datasets they added earlier (✕ next to each). Selecting 

2270 # the removed one falls back to the demo (see _remove_dataset). 

2271 if uploaded: 

2272 manage.caption("Remove an added dataset") 

2273 for name in uploaded: 

2274 name_col, x_col = manage.columns([5, 1]) 

2275 name_col.write(name) 

2276 x_col.button( 

2277 "✕", 

2278 key=f"remove_dataset_{name}", 

2279 on_click=_remove_dataset, 

2280 args=(name,), 

2281 help=f"Remove '{name}'", 

2282 ) 

2283 manage.caption( 

2284 "Have a public corpus? " 

2285 f"[Get it built in ↗]({CITATION['docs_url']}contributing-a-dataset/)" 

2286 )

2288 

2289def resolve_source_monitor( 

2290 data_choice: Optional[str], 

2291 words: pd.DataFrame, 

2292 fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2293) -> Tuple[int, int, bool]: 

2294 """The presentation monitor for a data source: ``(width, height, authoritative)``. 

2295 

2296 Lifted out of `seed_canvas_state` by **CMP-8 §1** so there is *one* source → 

2297 monitor table rather than two. `authoritative` keeps its meaning: the source 

2298 declares a real presentation monitor, so the canvas should snap to it rather 

2299 than to data-derived extents (which undershoot, because text rarely fills the 

2300 screen). 

2301 

2302 A **stored upload** now answers for itself when it recorded a setup snapshot 

2303 — before CMP-8 it declared nothing, so switching to one silently left the 

2304 canvas on the *previous* source's monitor. 

2305 """ 

2306 # OneStop server bundle + bundled demo share the same experimental setup 

2307 # (Dell U2715H, 2560x1440). 

2308 if data_choice in (ONESTOP_CHOICE, DEMO_CHOICE): 

2309 return 2560, 1440, True 

2310 if (monitor := _public_dataset_monitor(data_choice)) is not None: 

2311 return monitor[0], monitor[1], True 

2312 # A public corpus reached by its own registry *label* rather than through the 

2313 # `Public datasets` picker still declares a monitor — `_public_dataset_monitor` 

2314 # only answers for `PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE`, but `data_source_choice` holds the 

2315 # label (DATA-9's flat picker) and `compare_source` names B by label too. 

2316 # `active_setup_snapshot` already compensates; without the same fallback here a 

2317 # public corpus fell through to `compute_canvas_size` and reported its rounded 

2318 # data extents as an ESTIMATED canvas. Cosmetic before CMP-11 (only the split 

2319 # panels' `canvas_b` read it); load-bearing now that `setups_comparable` gates 

2320 # the overlay on the canvas, since it refused the very pairs CMP-11 exists to 

2321 # allow — and it also made A's resolution scan the whole corpus per rerun. 

2322 if declared := (PUBLIC_DATASET_REGISTRY.get(data_choice) or {}).get("monitor"): 

2323 return int(declared[0]), int(declared[1]), True 

2324 if data_choice == MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE: 

2325 # MultiplEYE server bundle = the same native MultiplEYE export as the 

2326 # public source; coordinates are offset onto the centered stimulus on 

2327 # the real 1920x1080 monitor, so snap the canvas to it (true-to-scale), 

2328 # exactly like the public MultiplEYE registry entry's monitor. 

2329 from scanpath_studio.datasets import MULTIPLEYE_MONITOR 

2330 

2331 return MULTIPLEYE_MONITOR[0], MULTIPLEYE_MONITOR[1], True 

2332 stored = (st.session_state.get("_datasets") or {}).get(data_choice) 

2333 if isinstance(stored, dict) and isinstance(stored.get("setup"), dict): 

2334 snapshot = SetupSnapshot.from_dict(stored["setup"], fallback=SetupSnapshot()) 

2335 # Authoritative only when the screen was actually *known*: an assumed or 

2336 # estimated canvas must not snap over a canvas the user has since tuned. 

2337 return ( 

2338 snapshot.canvas_width, 

2339 snapshot.canvas_height, 

2340 snapshot.screen_provenance is Provenance.MEASURED, 

2341 ) 

2342 if data_choice is None or data_choice == UPLOAD_CHOICE: 

2343 # Uploaded data (the setup wizard passes data_choice=None) defaults to a 

2344 # common 1440p monitor until the Recording-setup step says otherwise. 

2345 return DEFAULT_FIGURE_SIZE[0], DEFAULT_FIGURE_SIZE[1], False 

2346 derived_w, derived_h = compute_canvas_size(words, fixations) 

2347 return derived_w, derived_h, False 

2348 

2349 

2350def capture_setup_snapshot( 

2351 provenance: Optional[Mapping[str, Provenance]] = None, 

2352) -> SetupSnapshot: 

2353 """The resolved ``global_*`` geometry as a `SetupSnapshot` (CMP-8 §1). 

2354 

2355 Reads the same keys `seed_canvas_state` resolves, so there is no second list 

2356 of key names to keep in sync. ``provenance`` overrides the per-group 

2357 provenance — the wizard passes what the user answered; a built-in corpus that 

2358 declares its own monitor passes ``MEASURED``. 

2359 """ 

2360 ss = st.session_state 

2361 base = SetupSnapshot() 

2362 groups = dict(base.provenance) 

2363 groups.update(provenance or {}) 

2364 return SetupSnapshot( 

2365 canvas_width=int(ss.get("global_canvas_width", base.canvas_width)), 

2366 canvas_height=int(ss.get("global_canvas_height", base.canvas_height)), 

2367 monitor_width_mm=float( 

2368 ss.get("global_monitor_width_mm", base.monitor_width_mm) 

2369 ), 

2370 viewing_distance_mm=float( 

2371 ss.get("global_viewing_distance_mm", base.viewing_distance_mm) 

2372 ), 

2373 base_font_size=int(ss.get("global_base_font_size", base.base_font_size)), 

2374 font_family=str(ss.get("global_font_family", base.font_family)), 

2375 line_spacing=float(ss.get("global_line_spacing", base.line_spacing)), 

2376 scale_text_to_boxes=bool( 

2377 ss.get("global_scale_text_to_boxes", base.scale_text_to_boxes) 

2378 ), 

2379 screen_provenance=groups["screen"], 

2380 geometry_provenance=groups["geometry"], 

2381 text_provenance=groups["text"], 

2382 ) 

2383 

2384 

2385def active_setup_snapshot( 

2386 data_choice: Optional[str] = None, 

2387) -> Optional[SetupSnapshot]: 

2388 """A source's recorded setup, or ``None`` when it has none. 

2389 

2390 A stored upload carries the snapshot the wizard captured; a built-in corpus 

2391 that declares a monitor reports it as ``MEASURED``; anything else has nothing 

2392 to say, and saying nothing is the honest answer (a caller must not print 

2393 "assumed 2560x1440" for a corpus that never claimed one). 

2394 

2395 ``data_choice`` defaults to the active source, but callers that already know 

2396 which source they are describing — `_build_share_query` is handed one — 

2397 should pass it rather than re-reading session state. 

2398 """ 

2399 choice = ( 

2400 data_choice 

2401 if data_choice is not None 

2402 else st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") 

2403 ) 

2404 stored = (st.session_state.get("_datasets") or {}).get(choice) 

2405 if isinstance(stored, dict) and isinstance(stored.get("setup"), dict): 

2406 return SetupSnapshot.from_dict(stored["setup"], fallback=SetupSnapshot()) 

2407 declared = ( 

2408 choice in (ONESTOP_CHOICE, DEMO_CHOICE, MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE) 

2409 or _public_dataset_monitor(choice) is not None 

2410 # A public corpus reached by its own label (the DATA-3 OneStop source) 

2411 # rather than through the `Public datasets` picker still declares a 

2412 # monitor in the registry. 

2413 or bool((PUBLIC_DATASET_REGISTRY.get(choice) or {}).get("monitor")) 

2414 ) 

2415 if declared: 

2416 return capture_setup_snapshot( 

2417 { 

2418 # The corpus declares its presentation monitor, so the screen is 

2419 # measured. The physical size / viewing distance are *not* — no 

2420 # registry entry records them, so they stay honestly "assumed". 

2421 "screen": Provenance.MEASURED, 

2422 "geometry": Provenance.ASSUMED, 

2423 "text": Provenance.MEASURED, 

2424 } 

2425 ) 

2426 payload = st.session_state.get("_wizard_setup_snapshot") 

2427 if isinstance(payload, dict): 

2428 return SetupSnapshot.from_dict(payload, fallback=SetupSnapshot()) 

2429 return None 

2430 

2431 

2432def seed_canvas_state( 

2433 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2434 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2435 data_choice: Optional[str] = None, 

2436) -> Tuple[int, int, int, str, float, bool]: 

2437 """Resolve the canvas / typography settings without rendering any widget. 

2438 

2439 Split out of `render_sidebar_canvas_controls` by **VIZ-31**, which moved that 

2440 panel from the sidebar into the Scanpath rail. The rail renders inside 

2441 `tabs.render_single_trial_tab`, i.e. *after* `main` has to know the canvas 

2442 size and font in order to build `viz_settings` and dispatch a view — and the 

2443 Corpus view has no rail at all. This function does every session-state write 

2444 the panel used to do on its way past (source-driven monitor/font snapping and 

2445 the default seeding), then reads the resolved values back out, so both 

2446 callers agree and neither has to render to learn them. 

2447 

2448 Seeding is `controls._pin` (a plain default-if-absent); what keeps these 

2449 keys alive on a view that never renders their widgets is the widgets' own 

2450 `persist_state="session"` — see the comment on that block. 

2451 

2452 Returns: 

2453 Tuple of (canvas_width, canvas_height, base_font_size, font_family, 

2454 line_spacing, scale_text_to_boxes). The text-sizing pair keeps the reading 

2455 text true-to-scale: see `plots._word_label_font_px`. 

2456 """ 

2457 # OneStop server bundle + bundled demo share the same experimental setup 

2458 # (Dell U2715H, 2560x1440). Data-derived extents undershoot — text only 

2459 # fills part of the screen — so hard-default to the real monitor here. 

2460 # ``monitor_is_authoritative`` = the source declares a real presentation 

2461 # monitor (OneStop/demo or a public-dataset registry entry), so the canvas 

2462 # should snap to it rather than to data-derived extents. 

2463 default_canvas_w, default_canvas_h, monitor_is_authoritative = ( 

2464 resolve_source_monitor(data_choice, words_filtered, fixations_filtered) 

2465 ) 

2466 canvas_width = min(max(default_canvas_w, 100), 10000) 

2467 canvas_height = min(max(default_canvas_h, 100), 10000) 

2468 # Seed the data-derived defaults so the inputs render without a `value=` 

2469 # argument — that keeps the keys assignable by the plot-config restore 

2470 # (app._restore_plot_config) without Streamlit's "default value but also set 

2471 # via Session State API" warning. 

2472 # 

2473 # For a source with an authoritative monitor, snap the canvas to it whenever 

2474 # that source *changes* (selecting a public dataset, switching PoTeC↔MultiplEYE, 

2475 # or a public dataset whose registered monitor was updated): a plain 

2476 # ``setdefault`` would let a previously-seeded canvas stick, so a returning 

2477 # session would keep the old monitor and render the corpus off-scale. Manual 

2478 # canvas edits and plot-config restores within the same source are preserved 

2479 # (the key is unchanged, so the snap doesn't re-fire). 

2480 source_key = (data_choice, st.session_state.get("public_dataset_choice")) 

2481 if monitor_is_authoritative and st.session_state.get("_canvas_seeded_for") != ( 

2482 source_key 

2483 ): 

2484 st.session_state["global_canvas_width"] = canvas_width 

2485 st.session_state["global_canvas_height"] = canvas_height 

2486 st.session_state["_canvas_seeded_for"] = source_key 

2487 # The canvas pair itself is pinned with the rest of the defaults below. 

2488 

2489 # Authoritative reading font: MultiplEYE stamps the stimulus FONT_SIZE + family 

2490 # from its config onto the words. Snap the font controls to it when the source 

2491 # changes (same gate as the canvas), so the reading text renders at the exact 

2492 # size and (CJK) typeface the stimulus images were drawn with. We also turn off 

2493 # "scale text to boxes" since the precise px is known — box geometry can only 

2494 # approximate it. Manual edits within a source stick (the key is unchanged, so 

2495 # the snap doesn't re-fire); a returning source re-snaps to the known font. 

2496 font_px, font_css = _dataset_font(words_filtered) 

2497 if font_px is not None and st.session_state.get("_font_seeded_for") != source_key: 

2498 st.session_state["global_base_font_size"] = int(min(max(round(font_px), 6), 72)) 

2499 if font_css: 

2500 st.session_state["global_font_family"] = font_css 

2501 st.session_state["global_scale_text_to_boxes"] = False 

2502 st.session_state["_font_seeded_for"] = source_key 

2503 

2504 # The remaining widget defaults. Each of these used to be `setdefault`ed 

2505 # inline, immediately above its own widget; seeding them here is what lets a 

2506 # caller resolve the settings without rendering the panel. 

2507 # 

2508 # Seeding alone is NOT what keeps these alive. Since VIZ-31 these widgets 

2509 # render only in the Scanpath rail, and Streamlit drops a widget's key from 

2510 # session state at the end of any run in which the widget did not render — so 

2511 # one trip through **Corpus Analysis** (no rail) would prune all fourteen and 

2512 # the next run would seed the factory default over the user's canvas, font, 

2513 # text colour and background, permanently. What prevents that is 

2514 # `persist_state="session"` on each of those widgets (ENG-36; it replaced a 

2515 # hand-rolled re-assert-every-run workaround). Six of the fourteen are 

2516 # share-link / saved-config wire format, so this is not cosmetic. Pinned by 

2517 # `test_canvas_settings_survive_a_corpus_analysis_round_trip`. 

2518 ss = st.session_state 

2519 bg_options = list(BACKGROUND_PRESETS.keys()) + ["Custom…"] 

2520 if ss.get("global_bg_choice") not in bg_options: 

2521 ss.pop("global_bg_choice", None) 

2522 # One table drives both the pin and the read-back. `_pin` swallows the 

2523 # StreamlitAPIException raised when a key's widget was already built earlier 

2524 # in the run, so a pinned key is *not* guaranteed to land — every read below 

2525 # therefore goes through `_resolved`, never `ss[...]`, or a swallowed write 

2526 # would surface as a KeyError that takes the whole app down. 

2527 defaults = { 

2528 "global_canvas_width": canvas_width, 

2529 "global_canvas_height": canvas_height, 

2530 "global_monitor_width_mm": 597.0, 

2531 "global_viewing_distance_mm": 800.0, 

2532 "global_scale_text_to_boxes": True, 

2533 "global_line_spacing": float(DEFAULT_LINE_SPACING), 

2534 "global_base_font_size": 16, 

2535 "global_stimulus_font_pt": 12.0, 

2536 "global_use_stimulus_font_pt": False, 

2537 "global_font_family": FONT_FAMILY, 

2538 "global_text_color": WORD_LABEL_COLOR, 

2539 "global_bg_choice": bg_options[0], 

2540 # Pinned here as well as in the render path: its picker exists only while 

2541 # the choice is "Custom…", so it is the one key with no other keeper — 

2542 # without this a custom background is lost the first time the user opens 

2543 # Corpus Analysis and the choice silently falls back to a preset. 

2544 "global_bg_custom": DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR, 

2545 } 

2546 

2547 def _resolved(key): 

2548 return ss.get(key, defaults[key]) 

2549 

2550 for key, default in defaults.items(): 

2551 _pin(key, default) 

2552 # Derived from the two above it, so it is pinned after them. 

2553 _pin( 

2554 "global_display_dpi", 

2555 round( 

2556 float(_resolved("global_canvas_width")) 

2557 / (float(_resolved("global_monitor_width_mm")) / 25.4), 

2558 2, 

2559 ), 

2560 ) 

2561 # Point-specified stimulus typography converts to px through the DPI above. 

2562 # The rendering path recomputes this from its own widget values (which is 

2563 # what makes an edit apply the same run); this keeps the non-rendering 

2564 # callers on the same number. 

2565 if not _resolved("global_scale_text_to_boxes") and _resolved( 

2566 "global_use_stimulus_font_pt" 

2567 ): 

2568 ss["global_base_font_size"] = int( 

2569 min( 

2570 max( 

2571 round( 

2572 font_pt_to_px( 

2573 float(_resolved("global_stimulus_font_pt")), 

2574 float(ss.get("global_display_dpi", 96.0)), 

2575 ) 

2576 ), 

2577 6, 

2578 ), 

2579 72, 

2580 ) 

2581 ) 

2582 return ( 

2583 int(_resolved("global_canvas_width")), 

2584 int(_resolved("global_canvas_height")), 

2585 int(_resolved("global_base_font_size")), 

2586 str(_resolved("global_font_family")), 

2587 float(_resolved("global_line_spacing")), 

2588 bool(_resolved("global_scale_text_to_boxes")), 

2589 ) 

2590 

2591 

2592def render_sidebar_canvas_controls( 

2593 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2594 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2595 data_choice: Optional[str] = None, 

2596 slot=None, 

2597 expanded: bool = False, 

2598 title: str = "Experimental Setup", 

2599 bare: bool = False, 

2600) -> Tuple[int, int, int, str, float, bool]: 

2601 """Render the canvas-geometry, typography and background panel. 

2602 

2603 These controls let the user match the visualization to the experimental 

2604 display, which is what keeps coordinates and word boxes spatially accurate. 

2605 

2606 The panel normally renders into ``slot`` as its own collapsible expander. 

2607 Pass ``bare=True`` when ``slot`` is already the disclosure container, as the 

2608 compact Scanpath rail does. The setup wizard keeps the standalone expander. 

2609 `seed_canvas_state` does the state work and is called first here, so rendering 

2610 and not-rendering resolve identically. 

2611 

2612 **UX-48 sub-grouping.** In ``bare`` mode these ~19 controls share the rail's 

2613 "📐 Figure & canvas" disclosure with the axes/label controls, which made one 

2614 ~26-row scroll with no internal structure. So the compact form splits them 

2615 into two popovers — **🖥️ Screen & geometry** (the monitor the experiment ran 

2616 on) and **🔤 Text & fonts** (how the reading text is drawn, plus the two 

2617 colours) — the same `expander → popover` shape every layer group uses. The 

2618 wizard's standalone expander stays flat: that step *is* the setup form, and 

2619 hiding half of it behind buttons would be a step you can't read at a glance. 

2620 

2621 Returns: 

2622 Tuple of (canvas_width, canvas_height, base_font_size, font_family, 

2623 line_spacing, scale_text_to_boxes). 

2624 """ 

2625 seed_canvas_state(words_filtered, fixations_filtered, data_choice) 

2626 _, font_css = _dataset_font(words_filtered) 

2627 host = slot if slot is not None else st.container() 

2628 display = host if bare else host.expander(title, expanded=expanded) 

2629 

2630 def field(host, kind: str, label: str, **kwargs): 

2631 """One control, `label | field` in the rail and label-above in the wizard. 

2632 

2633 UX-51 made the rail read as a compact form; the wizard's flat expander 

2634 keeps the label above its field, for the same reason it stays flat — that 

2635 step *is* the setup form, laid out across the page rather than inside a 

2636 28rem popover, so there is no height to buy back. 

2637 """ 

2638 if bare: 

2639 return _labeled(host, kind, label, **kwargs) 

2640 kwargs.pop("display", None) 

2641 return getattr(host, kind)(label, **kwargs) 

2642 

2643 # Both sub-groups are created up front (Streamlit lays containers out in 

2644 # creation order), so the code below keeps its order while landing in the 

2645 # right group. Flat mode points both names at the one container.

2647 display.popover("🖥️ Screen & geometry", width="stretch") if bare else display 

2648 )

2650 canvas_width = field( 

2651 screen, 

2652 "number_input",

2663 "number_input",

2699 display_dpi = field( 

2700 screen, 

2701 "number_input",

2724 scale_text_to_boxes = text.checkbox(

2764 ) 

2765 if not scale_text_to_boxes and use_stimulus_font_pt: 

2766 st.session_state["global_base_font_size"] = int(

2768 ) 

2769 base_font_size = field( 

2770 text, 

2771 "number_input", 

2772 "Figure font size (px)",

2774 max_value=72, 

2775 step=1, 

2776 help="Real (monitor-pixel) font size, scaled true-to-scale with the "

2779 key="global_base_font_size", 

2780 persist_state="session", 

2781 disabled=not scale_text_to_boxes and use_stimulus_font_pt, 

2782 ) 

2783 # VIZ-1: every font-size control here is in pixels, but stimulus typography 

2784 # is usually specified in points. Spell out the difference + the conversion. 

2785 text.caption( 

2786 "ℹ️ Font sizes here are in **pixels (px)**, but stimuli are usually " 

2787 "specified in **points (pt)**. To match the original, convert via the " 

2788 "experiment's DPI: `px = pt × DPI ÷ 72` (e.g. 12 pt ≈ 16 px at 96 DPI). " 

2789 "Prefer **Scale text to boxes** when the data ships word boxes — it sizes " 

2790 "the text from the real geometry and sidesteps the conversion." 

2791 ) 

2792 text.button( 

2793 "Use multilingual font stack", 

2794 on_click=lambda: st.session_state.update( 

2795 global_font_family=( 

2796 "'Noto Sans', 'Noto Sans Hebrew', 'Noto Sans Arabic', " 

2797 "'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Arial Unicode MS', sans-serif" 

2798 ) 

2799 ), 

2800 help="A CJK/Hebrew/Arabic-capable CSS fallback stack (PRE-6).", 

2801 ) 

2802 font_family = field( 

2803 text, 

2804 "text_input", 

2805 "Text font", 

2806 key="global_font_family", 

2807 persist_state="session", 

2808 help="Font for the word labels. Use the exact font from your experiment " 

2809 "(e.g. 'Courier New') or a CSS fallback stack.", 

2810 ) 

2811 if "right_to_left" in words_filtered and words_filtered["right_to_left"].any(): 

2812 text.caption( 

2813 "↔ RTL script detected. Landing positions are measured from the " 

2814 "logical word start; browser bidi shaping is used for labels." 

2815 ) 

2816 # When the dataset declares its stimulus typeface (MultiplEYE), the overlaid 

2817 # text only lines up with the stimulus image if that exact font is installed 

2818 # on the viewer's machine — we don't bundle it, and the browser otherwise 

2819 # falls back per-script (CJK lands, but half-width Latin in a CJK font drifts, 

2820 # e.g. URLs render too wide). Tell the user the font + how to get it. 

2821 hint = _stimulus_font_install_hint(font_css) 

2822 if hint is not None: 

2823 font_name, font_url = hint

2826 "to match the stimulus image exactly, install that font on this " 

2827 "computer (it isn't bundled), then reload — otherwise the browser " 

2828 "substitutes a fallback and labels (especially URLs / Latin) can " 

2829 f"drift. [Download]({font_url}); install via Font Book (macOS), " 

2830 "right-click → Install (Windows), or `~/.local/share/fonts` + " 

2831 "`fc-cache -f` (Linux). Or just turn on the **stimulus image** to read " 

2832 "the original text." 

2833 )

2848 bg_options = list(BACKGROUND_PRESETS.keys()) + ["Custom…"] 

2849 field( 

2850 text, 

2851 "selectbox",

2862 # This picker exists only while the choice is "Custom…", so it typically 

2863 # FIRST mounts on a later run — the BUG-15 case, now handled by the 

2864 # widget's own `persist_state="session"` (ENG-36) rather than by 

2865 # re-asserting the value from Python on every run. 

2866 _pin("global_bg_custom", DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR) 

2867 field( 

2868 text, 

2869 "color_picker", 

2870 "Custom background color", 

2871 display="Custom colour", 

2872 key="global_bg_custom", 

2873 persist_state="session", 

2874 ) 

2875 

2876 return (

2878 int(canvas_height), 

2879 int(base_font_size), 

2880 font_family,

2891def _render_authoring_source() -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: 

2892 """Standalone editor whose result joins the ordinary plot/export pipeline.""" 

2893 from scanpath_studio.authoring import ( 

2894 DEFAULT_LAYOUT, 

2895 apply_authoring_event, 

2896 authored_fixations, 

2897 authoring_json, 

2898 default_events, 

2899 event_problems, 

2900 layout_text, 

2901 layout_problems, 

2902 parse_authoring_document, 

2903 reconcile_event_table, 

2904 unusable_event_rows, 

2905 ) 

2906 from scanpath_studio.authoring_component import render_authoring_canvas 

2907 

2908 st.subheader("✏️ Author a scanpath") 

2909 st.caption( 

2910 "Write the stimulus, then click or drag directly on the canvas. X/Y are " 

2911 "the primary authored values; the optional target word is useful for " 

2912 "measures but does not constrain where a fixation can be placed. The " 

2913 "numeric table remains a complete keyboard-accessible editor." 

2914 ) 

2915 restored = st.file_uploader( 

2916 "Restore authoring file", 

2917 type=["json"], 

2918 key="author_restore_upload", 

2919 help="Load a JSON file previously saved from this editor.", 

2920 ) 

2921 if restored is not None: 

2922 identity = (restored.name, restored.size) 

2923 if st.session_state.get("_author_restore_identity") != identity: 

2924 try: 

2925 document = parse_authoring_document(restored.getvalue().decode("utf-8")) 

2926 except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc: 

2927 st.error(str(exc)) 

2928 else: 

2929 st.session_state["author_text"] = document.text 

2930 st.session_state["_author_layout"] = document.layout 

2931 st.session_state["_authored_events_frame"] = document.events 

2932 st.session_state["_author_text_for_events"] = document.text 

2933 st.session_state["_author_selected_fixation"] = None 

2934 st.session_state["_author_events_editor_revision"] = ( 

2935 int(st.session_state.get("_author_events_editor_revision", 0)) + 1 

2936 ) 

2937 st.session_state["_author_restore_identity"] = identity 

2938 

2939 text = st.text_area( 

2940 "Stimulus text", 

2941 value="Reading unfolds through a sequence of careful eye movements.", 

2942 key="author_text", 

2943 height=100, 

2944 ) 

2945 layout = {**DEFAULT_LAYOUT, **st.session_state.get("_author_layout", {})} 

2946 words = layout_text(text, **layout) 

2947 with st.expander("Parsed word geometry", expanded=False): 

2948 if words.empty: 

2949 st.info( 

2950 "Enter stimulus text to create word boxes. The empty canvas is still valid." 

2951 ) 

2952 else: 

2953 line_count = int(words["line_idx"].max()) + 1 

2954 st.caption( 

2955 f"{len(words)} {'word' if len(words) == 1 else 'words'} across " 

2956 f"{line_count} {'line' if line_count == 1 else 'lines'} · word ids are " 

2957 "1-based; line indices are 0-based. Explicit blank lines are retained." 

2958 ) 

2959 st.dataframe( 

2960 words[["text", "word_id", "line_idx", "x", "y", "width", "height"]], 

2961 hide_index=True, 

2962 width="stretch", 

2963 ) 

2964 for problem in layout_problems( 

2965 words, canvas_width=layout["canvas_width"], margin=layout["margin"] 

2966 ): 

2967 st.warning(problem) 

2968 

2969 if st.session_state.get("_author_text_for_events") != text: 

2970 st.session_state["_authored_events_frame"] = default_events(words) 

2971 st.session_state["_author_events_editor_revision"] = ( 

2972 int(st.session_state.get("_author_events_editor_revision", 0)) + 1 

2973 ) 

2974 st.session_state["_author_text_for_events"] = text 

2975 st.session_state["_author_selected_fixation"] = None 

2976 seed = st.session_state.get("_authored_events_frame", default_events(words)) 

2977 last_word = int(words["word_id"].max()) if not words.empty else 1 

2978 canvas_panel = st.container() 

2979 fixation_table = st.expander("Fixation table", expanded=False) 

2980 fixation_table.caption( 

2981 "One row per fixation. **Fixation id** is stable; **Order** controls the " 

2982 "reading sequence. X/Y place the marker in screen pixels. **Target word** " 

2983 f"is optional (1–{last_word}) and may be edited independently; blank X/Y " 

2984 "fall back to that word's centre." 

2985 ) 

2986 # BUG-19: the editor's own key holds the edits as a delta against `seed`, so 

2987 # `seed` must stay the STABLE base — it is reseeded only when the stimulus 

2988 # text changes or a file is restored. Writing the returned frame back into it 

2989 # applies that delta twice, and after a row deletion leaves a gapped index, 

2990 # which `num_rows="dynamic"` cannot add rows to: from there edits land on the 

2991 # wrong rows and rows disappear. Read the edits from the return value only. 

2992 editor_revision = int(st.session_state.get("_author_events_editor_revision", 0)) 

2993 events = fixation_table.data_editor( 

2994 seed, 

2995 key=f"author_events_editor_{editor_revision}", 

2996 num_rows="dynamic", 

2997 hide_index=True, 

2998 column_config={ 

2999 "fixation_id": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3000 "Fixation id", 

3001 disabled=True, 

3002 help="Stable marker identity used to synchronize canvas and table edits.", 

3003 ), 

3004 "order_in_trial": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3005 "Order", 

3006 min_value=1, 

3007 step=1, 

3008 help="Reading order. Each fixation needs a unique whole number.", 

3009 ), 

3010 "word_id": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3011 "Target word (optional)", 

3012 min_value=1, 

3013 max_value=last_word, 

3014 step=1, 

3015 help=( 

3016 "Optional measure target, counting from 1. It does not move " 

3017 "the marker or change X/Y." 

3018 ), 

3019 ), 

3020 "x": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3021 "X (px)", 

3022 help="Horizontal screen coordinate; independent of target word.", 

3023 ), 

3024 "y": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3025 "Y (px)", help="Vertical screen coordinate; independent of target word." 

3026 ), 

3027 "duration_ms": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3028 "Duration (ms)", 

3029 min_value=1, 

3030 help="How long the fixation lasts. It also sets the marker size.", 

3031 ), 

3032 }, 

3033 width="stretch", 

3034 ) 

3035 selected = st.session_state.get("_author_selected_fixation") 

3036 try: 

3037 effective_events, selected = reconcile_event_table(events, selected) 

3038 except ValueError as exc: 

3039 st.error(f"Fix the event table before these edits can be drawn or saved: {exc}") 

3040 effective_events, selected = reconcile_event_table(seed, selected) 

3041 events_valid = False 

3042 else: 

3043 events_valid = True 

3044 st.session_state["_author_selected_fixation"] = selected 

3045 

3046 for problem in event_problems(words, events): 

3047 if not problem.startswith(("Fixation id", "Order")): 

3048 st.warning(problem) 

3049 dropped = unusable_event_rows(words, events) 

3050 if dropped: 

3051 st.caption( 

3052 "Rows without finite X/Y or a valid target are not drawn until corrected." 

3053 ) 

3054 

3055 canvas_height = max( 

3056 480, 

3057 int(words["y"].max() + words["height"].max() + layout["margin"]) 

3058 if not words.empty 

3059 else 480, 

3060 ) 

3061 with canvas_panel: 

3062 canvas_event = render_authoring_canvas( 

3063 words, 

3064 effective_events, 

3065 canvas_width=layout["canvas_width"], 

3066 canvas_height=canvas_height, 

3067 selected_fixation_id=selected, 

3068 ) 

3069 if canvas_event: 

3070 try: 

3071 updated, selected = apply_authoring_event( 

3072 effective_events, 

3073 canvas_event, 

3074 selected_fixation_id=selected, 

3075 ) 

3076 except ValueError as exc: 

3077 st.error(str(exc)) 

3078 else: 

3079 st.session_state["_authored_events_frame"] = updated 

3080 st.session_state["_author_selected_fixation"] = selected 

3081 # A data editor's browser delta is keyed against the frame it first 

3082 # mounted with. Give canvas-authored data a fresh key so the visible 

3083 # table mounts from the new coordinates instead of retaining its old 

3084 # client-side base (the same invariant as BUG-19, in the other 

3085 # direction). 

3086 st.session_state["_author_events_editor_revision"] = editor_revision + 1 

3087 st.rerun() 

3088 

3089 st.download_button( 

3090 "💾 Save authoring file", 

3091 data=authoring_json(text, effective_events, layout=layout), 

3092 file_name="authored-scanpath.json", 

3093 mime="application/json", 

3094 disabled=not events_valid, 

3095 ) 

3096 return words, authored_fixations(words, effective_events) 

3097 

3098 

3099#: PRE-1 control defaults. These keys are a wire format — a deep link or a saved 

3100#: config writes them into session state via `url_state` *before* the widgets 

3101#: render, so the widgets must NOT also pass `value=`: Streamlit warns when a 

3102#: keyed widget is given both (BUG-17). A plain `setdefault` is enough here (the 

3103#: expander's contents render every run, so these never mount late — unlike the 

3104#: `persist_state` cases above); see `controls._pin` for that distinction. 

3105#: Keep in sync with the fallbacks in `url_state._restore_plot_config` and 

3106#: `tabs._build_studio_config`. 

3107_PREPROC_DEFAULTS: dict = { 

3108 "global_preproc_enabled": False, 

3109 "global_preproc_short_policy": "Off", 

3110 "global_preproc_short_threshold_ms": 80.0, 

3111 "global_preproc_merge_distance_chars": 1.0, 

3112 "global_preproc_blink_adjacent": True, 

3113} 

3114 

3115 

3116def _preprocessing_settings(host=None) -> dict: 

3117 """Render the PRE-1 controls and return their cache-key-safe settings. 

3118 

3119 ``host`` is the 🧹 Preprocessing section of the Data page (DATA-26). Renders 

3120 bare into it — the section heading is the page's, written into the slot above 

3121 these widgets by ``main``. 

3122 

3123 It belongs on the page rather than in the Scanpath rail (where UX-38 floated 

3124 putting it) because ``app._preprocessing_settings`` reshapes the frames 

3125 *every* view reads, including Corpus Analysis, which has no rail: a 

3126 dataset-wide control must not be unreachable from one of the views it 

3127 changes. 

3128 """ 

3129 for key, default in _PREPROC_DEFAULTS.items(): 

3130 st.session_state.setdefault(key, default) 

3131 with host if host is not None else st.container(): 

3132 enabled = st.toggle( 

3133 "Enable preprocessing", 

3134 key="global_preproc_enabled", 

3135 persist_state="session", 

3136 help="Optional and off by default. Original rows remain available; " 

3137 "excluded rows are soft-marked with a reason.", 

3138 ) 

3139 policy = st.selectbox( 

3140 "Short fixations", 

3141 ["Off", "Merge", "Merge then discard", "Discard"], 

3142 key="global_preproc_short_policy", 

3143 persist_state="session", 

3144 disabled=not enabled, 

3145 ) 

3146 threshold = st.number_input( 

3147 "Short threshold (ms)", 

3148 min_value=1.0, 

3149 max_value=500.0, 

3150 key="global_preproc_short_threshold_ms", 

3151 persist_state="session", 

3152 disabled=not enabled or policy == "Off", 

3153 ) 

3154 distance = st.number_input( 

3155 "Merge distance (characters)", 

3156 min_value=0.25, 

3157 max_value=10.0, 

3158 step=0.25, 

3159 key="global_preproc_merge_distance_chars", 

3160 persist_state="session", 

3161 disabled=not enabled or "Merge" not in policy, 

3162 ) 

3163 blink = st.toggle( 

3164 "Exclude blink-adjacent fixations", 

3165 key="global_preproc_blink_adjacent", 

3166 persist_state="session", 

3167 disabled=not enabled, 

3168 ) 

3169 if st.button("Recompute preprocessing", disabled=not enabled): 

3170 st.cache_data.clear() 

3171 return { 

3172 "enabled": enabled, 

3173 "short_policy": policy, 

3174 "short_threshold_ms": threshold, 

3175 "merge_distance_chars": distance, 

3176 "discard_blink_adjacent": blink, 

3177 } 

3178 

3179 

3180def _activate_data_source(data_choice: str, *, preproc_host=None) -> dict: 

3181 """Reset source-scoped state and return the active preprocessing settings. 

3182 

3183 ``preproc_host`` is the 🧹 Preprocessing section of the Data page (DATA-26 — 

3184 it was a popover on the top menu bar until the page took it). 

3185 """ 

3186 st.session_state["_active_data_source"] = data_choice 

3187 preprocessing = _preprocessing_settings(preproc_host) 

3188 if st.session_state.get("_share_selection_source") != data_choice: 

3189 st.session_state.pop("_share_selection", None) 

3190 st.session_state["_share_selection_source"] = data_choice 

3191 

3192 source_key = (data_choice, st.session_state.get("public_dataset_choice")) 

3193 if st.session_state.get("_filters_for") == source_key: 

3194 return preprocessing 

3195 

3196 previous = st.session_state.get("_filters_for") 

3197 stash = st.session_state.setdefault("_filter_stash", {}) 

3198 if previous is not None: 

3199 stash[previous] = dict(st.session_state.get("_trial_filters_raw", {})) 

3200 stale_keys = [ 

3201 key 

3202 for key in st.session_state 

3203 if isinstance(key, str) and key.startswith("filter_") 

3204 ] 

3205 for key in stale_keys: 

3206 del st.session_state[key] 

3207 st.session_state.pop("_trial_filters", None) 

3208 restored = stash.get(source_key) 

3209 st.session_state["_trial_filters_raw"] = dict(restored) if restored else {} 

3210 st.session_state["_filters_for"] = source_key 

3211 return preprocessing 

3212 

3213 

3214def main() -> None: 

3215 """Main application entry point. 

3216 

3217 Orchestrates the full application workflow: 

3218 1. Configure Streamlit page and custom CSS 

3219 2. Render title and caption 

3220 3. Load and normalize data (words, fixations, optional raw gaze) 

3221 4. Apply user-selected filters (participants, trials, texts) 

3222 5. Render sidebar controls (canvas, fonts, visualization settings) 

3223 6. Render the active view (Scanpath Visualization / Corpus Analysis / Data Inspection) 

3224 

3225 Data Flow: 

3226 CSV upload → schema inference → normalization → filtering → 

3227 trial combination building → visualization rendering 

3228 

3229 UI Structure: 

3230 Sidebar: Data source, filters, canvas settings, viz controls 

3231 Main area: 4 tabs for different views of the data 

3232 

3233 Error Handling: 

3234 - Stops execution if schema inference fails 

3235 - Shows warning if filtering eliminates all data 

3236 - Handles missing raw gaze data gracefully 

3237 """ 

3238 configure_page() 

3239 # PERF-3: the cache-key memo is scoped to ONE script run — drop last run's 

3240 # entries before anything fingerprints a frame, so a frame rebuilt this run 

3241 # is hashed afresh and last run's frames stop being kept alive. 

3242 reset_fingerprint_memo() 

3243 # Start capturing log records into the in-app debug buffer before any data 

3244 # or plot work runs, so the debug panel (?debug=1) sees this run's logs. 

3245 install_log_capture() 

3246 # Apply deep-link presets BEFORE any widget renders — see _apply_url_preset 

3247 # for the full URL schema. External tools can deep-link into this app with 

3248 # `?source=...&participant=...&trial=...&...` to land on a specific trial 

3249 # with the reviewer's preferred viz settings. 

3250 url_source = _apply_url_preset() 

3251 # ENG-26: desktop/localhost installs remember uploaded datasets, annotations, 

3252 # mappings and view settings across browser refreshes and process restarts. 

3253 # Public deployments never opt in implicitly (there is no user identity with 

3254 # which to isolate the cache). URL presets are applied first and therefore 

3255 # win over restored settings; an explicit ?source= also wins over the stored 

3256 # data-source choice. 

3257 app_url = str(getattr(st.context, "url", "") or "") 

3258 if restore_local_state( 

3259 st.session_state, app_url, protect_data_source=url_source is not None 

3260 ): 

3261 # ENG-30: say it once, where the user is looking. Silently repopulating a 

3262 # session reads as "the app kept my data somewhere" without saying where; 

3263 # the toast points at the menu panel that answers that. 

3264 st.toast( 

3265 "Restored your last session from this computer — see 💾 Session → " 

3266 "🗄️ Recovery cache, beside the title.", 

3267 icon="↩️", 

3268 ) 

3269 if url_source == "onestop" and onestop_data_dir() is not None: 

3270 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", ONESTOP_CHOICE) 

3271 elif url_source == "multipleye" and multipleye_bundle_dir() is not None: 

3272 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE) 

3273 elif url_source == "demo": 

3274 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", DEMO_CHOICE) 

3275 elif url_source == "synthetic": 

3276 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", SYNTHETIC_CHOICE) 

3277 elif url_source == "author": 

3278 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", AUTHOR_CHOICE) 

3279 elif url_source == "onestop_public" and public_datasets_enabled(): 

3280 # DATA-3: the public OneStop corpus is shareable. Land on it in the flat 

3281 # picker; _apply_url_preset already seeded onestop_variant/regime/parts. 

3282 st.session_state.setdefault("data_source_choice", ONESTOP_PUBLIC_CHOICE) 

3283 elif url_source == "upload": 

3284 st.session_state.setdefault("_show_upload_wizard", True) 

3285 

3286 # Chrome first, page heading second: Streamlit's native top nav, then the 

3287 # settings menu bar, then the title. 

3288 # 

3289 # AFTER `restore_local_state`, deliberately: `render_nav` resolves the active 

3290 # view and writes `main_nav`, so running it earlier would pin the view to the 

3291 # router's default before the recovery cache could restore the one the user 

3292 # was last on. BEFORE any data loading, equally deliberately: the loaders' 

3293 # directory inputs, download buttons and column-mapping panels fill the bar's 

3294 # popovers by `host=`, so those slots have to exist first — the same 

3295 # reserve-then-fill discipline the sidebar containers had. 

3296 seed_debug_mode() # UX-37: a legacy ?debug=1 link pre-arms the Help toggle. 

3297 menu = render_top_menu(show_debug=debug_enabled()) 

3298 _render_about_panel(menu.title) 

3299 

3300 # First-visit welcome tour. After the URL presets, so embeds and 

3301 # deep-linked sessions can suppress it — but BEFORE the heavy data/plot 

3302 # work, so the welcome streams to the browser immediately instead of 

3303 # after the full first render. Replay clicks arm the tour in the button's 

3304 # on_click callback, which runs before this point in the rerun. 

3305 maybe_show_welcome_tour() 

3306 render_spotlight_tour() 

3307 # UX-40: task-oriented tutorials share the spotlight mechanism but keep 

3308 # their own progress and do not inherit the welcome tour's opt-out. 

3309 render_use_case_tutorial() 

3310 # UX-39: arm the title's easter egg. After the tour/tutorial renders, because 

3311 # its suppression reads the `tour_mode` / `tutorial_active` those set — and it 

3312 # doesn't care about DOM order, being a height-0 script that retries until the 

3313 # heading has hydrated. 

3314 render_easter_egg() 

3315 # UX-15: same deal for the FAQ dialog — the ❓ Help menu button that arms it 

3316 # renders at the bottom of this function, so serving it here is what keeps 

3317 # the modal from waiting out the whole rerun. Ditto ℹ️ About, a dialog since 

3318 # the menu bar made it a popover inside a popover. 

3319 maybe_show_faq() 

3320 maybe_show_about() 

3321 maybe_show_tutorial_library() 

3322 

3323 # Active top-level view (set by the nav switch). Read here so the dispatch 

3324 # below renders only the active page. 

3325 active_view = _active_view() 

3326 

3327 # Switching view is a full rerun — data load, filters, then a page of fresh 

3328 # figures — and Streamlit leaves the OLD view painted until the new run 

3329 # overwrites each element. So a click on "Corpus Analysis" left the scanpath 

3330 # sitting there, looking like nothing had happened. Paint a bridge the 

3331 # moment we know the view changed: it lands high on the page, before the 

3332 # slow work, so the click gets an immediate answer. Cleared just before the 

3333 # real view renders. Same pattern (and reasoning) as `_finalizing_bridge` 

3334 # above — see ENG-36 for why the message keeps its own line above the 

3335 # skeleton rather than relying on a bare skeleton to explain itself. 

3336 # 

3337 # The container is created on EVERY run, not only on a switch, and only 

3338 # *filled* on a switch. Streamlit reconciles the element tree by position: 

3339 # a run that skipped creating it left the previous run's banner + skeleton 

3340 # sitting there unclaimed, so the "Loading…" never went away. Always 

3341 # claiming the slot means the next run overwrites it with an empty 

3342 # container, which is what clears it. 

3343 # 

3344 # It has to be an `st.empty()` placeholder, not a plain container: 

3345 # `container.empty()` *appends* an empty child, it does not drop the 

3346 # children already written into it, so the banner and skeleton survived the 

3347 # clear below and sat above the finished page until some later rerun 

3348 # happened to redraw the slot. A placeholder holds exactly one element — a 

3349 # child container when there is something to say, nothing after `.empty()`. 

3350 _view_bridge = st.empty() 

3351 if st.session_state.get("_last_rendered_view") not in (None, active_view): 

3352 _bridge_box = _view_bridge.container() 

3353 _bridge_box.info(f"Loading {view_label(active_view)}…", icon="⏳") 

3354 _bridge_box.skeleton(height=420) 

3355 else: 

3356 _view_bridge = None 

3357 st.session_state["_last_rendered_view"] = active_view 

3358 

3359 # DATA-26 — the **Data** page ("Set up your dataset"). One place for 

3360 # everything about the dataset itself, instead of a ⚙️ Configure menu group 

3361 # at the top and a 🔎 Data Inspection subtab on the far side of the Scanpath 

3362 # view asking the same questions at two points in the pipeline. 

3363 # 

3364 # The page is built on EVERY run and merely hidden when another view is 

3365 # active (`DATA_PAGE_OFFSCREEN_KEY` → `display: none` in styles.py). That is 

3366 # not laziness: the slots below are filled by the loaders' directory input, 

3367 # ⬇ Download button, source options and column-mapping selectboxes, all of 

3368 # which *drive* `prepare_data` on every rerun — and Streamlit drops the key 

3369 # of a widget that did not render. Rendering-then-hiding keeps the popovers' 

3370 # every-run semantics exactly, so this stays a re-host rather than a rewrite 

3371 # of every loader into a render/resolve pair. 

3372 # 

3373 # Sub-slots are reserved in page order and filled at whatever point of the 

3374 # load reaches them (Streamlit lays containers out in creation order): 

3375 # Data source (picker + ➕ manage) 

3376 # Description (public-dataset caption / home link) 

3377 # Options (source-specific: OneStop regime + parts + variant, …) 

3378 # Data location (path input + Expected files + found/download status) 

3379 # Add a dataset (the upload wizard, while one is being added) 

3380 # What's in it (name + counts + raw tables + stats + trial identity) 

3381 # Column mapping (ONE section, three modes — see _render_setup_mapping) 

3382 # Participant metadata (DATA-20) 

3383 # Preprocessing 

3384 data_view = active_view == _VIEW_DATA 

3385 setup_page = st.container( 

3386 key=DATA_PAGE_KEY if data_view else DATA_PAGE_OFFSCREEN_KEY 

3387 ) 

3388 if data_view: 

3389 setup_page.header("Set up your dataset") 

3390 setup_page.caption( 

3391 "Where the data comes from, what is actually in it, how its columns " 

3392 "map onto the app's canonical fields, what you know about the " 

3393 "readers, and the optional preprocessing applied before anything is " 

3394 "measured." 

3395 ) 

3396 # UX-52 — four peer sections, one heading level, one divider between 

3397 # each. The source block used to open with no heading at all, which 

3398 # made the three headings below it read as the whole page rather than 

3399 # as three of its four stages. Written straight into `setup_page` 

3400 # before the slots are created, so it lands above them (Streamlit lays 

3401 # containers out in creation order). 

3402 setup_page.divider() 

3403 setup_page.subheader("📂 Data source") 

3404 setup_page.caption( 

3405 "Which dataset, where its files are, and any options that source offers." 

3406 ) 

3407 setup_source_slot = setup_page.container() 

3408 description_slot = setup_page.container() 

3409 source_options_slot = setup_page.container() 

3410 data_location_slot = setup_page.container() 

3411 setup_wizard_slot = setup_page.container() 

3412 # UX-52 round 2 — "what's in this dataset" comes **before** the mapping, on 

3413 # the user's call. It breaks pipeline order deliberately: the counts are the 

3414 # first thing you want after choosing a source ("did it load, and is it the 

3415 # right size?"), and the mapping is what you scroll to when the answer looks 

3416 # wrong. Reserving the slots in this order is the whole change — Streamlit 

3417 # lays containers out in creation order, so *when* each is filled during the 

3418 # load is unaffected. 

3419 setup_body_slot = setup_page.container() 

3420 # Keyed → the stable `.st-key-…` selectors the "Load and verify a dataset" 

3421 # tutorial spotlights (UX-40), alongside `tutorial_data_inspection` above. 

3422 column_mapping_slot = setup_page.container(key="tutorial_column_mapping") 

3423 # The heading belongs to the *section*, not to any one of its three modes — 

3424 # mode A's panels are written into the body by `prepare_data` during the 

3425 # load, long before the dispatch below picks a mode, so the title needs a 

3426 # slot of its own above them (see tabs._render_column_mapping_section). 

3427 mapping_head_slot = column_mapping_slot.container() 

3428 mapping_body_slot = column_mapping_slot.container() 

3429 # Raw tables for a dataset whose mapping is still broken. Its own slot, 

3430 # *below* the editor: with "what's in it" moved above, filling that one 

3431 # would put the tables above the controls that fix them. 

3432 unmapped_slot = setup_page.container() 

3433 # DATA-20 §1 — the participant-level metadata table. After the mapping (it 

3434 # joins on the reader id the mapping just settled). 

3435 setup_metadata_slot = setup_page.container(key="tutorial_participant_metadata") 

3436 setup_preproc_slot = setup_page.container(key="tutorial_preprocessing") 

3437 

3438 # Data source selection. UX-25: only the *resolution* happens here (it must 

3439 # precede the load); the picker itself renders in the main view — on the 

3440 # Scanpath "Filter by" row, at the top of the Corpus view, or (DATA-26) in 

3441 # the page slot above. The resolver takes the same slot because while the 

3442 # add-dataset wizard is open it renders a "✕ Cancel" bar *instead of* a 

3443 # picker, and rendering both would duplicate the `tour_grp_data_source` key. 

3444 data_choice = render_sidebar_data_source(host=setup_source_slot) 

3445 if data_view and data_choice != UPLOAD_CHOICE: 

3446 render_data_source_picker(host=setup_source_slot) 

3447 if data_view: 

3448 setup_preproc_slot.divider() 

3449 setup_preproc_slot.subheader("🧹 Preprocessing") 

3450 setup_preproc_slot.caption( 

3451 "Optional soft exclusion and merging of short fixations, applied to " 

3452 "every view. Off by default; original rows remain available." 

3453 ) 

3454 

3455 preproc_settings = _activate_data_source( 

3456 data_choice, preproc_host=setup_preproc_slot 

3457 ) 

3458 # Just-finalized upload: paint a "loading" bridge into the main area now so it 

3459 # repaints over the wizard (instead of the wizard lingering until the slow 

3460 # first figure finishes). Cleared just before the tabs render below. 

3461 # 

3462 # ENG-36: the message keeps its own line — a bare skeleton says "loading" but 

3463 # not *what*, and the wizard has just closed under the user — while 

3464 # `st.skeleton` (1.59) reserves the height the plot is about to take, so the 

3465 # page doesn't reflow when the figure lands. Standalone mode, not the `with` 

3466 # form: the wait spans everything between here and the tab render below, not 

3467 # one block. 

3468 # An `st.empty()` placeholder for the same reason as the view bridge above: 

3469 # `.empty()` on a plain container adds a child instead of clearing one. 

3470 _finalizing_bridge = None 

3471 if st.session_state.pop("_wizard_finalizing", False): 

3472 _finalizing_bridge = st.empty() 

3473 _finalizing_box = _finalizing_bridge.container() 

3474 _finalizing_box.info("✅ Dataset added — loading your scanpaths…", icon="⏳") 

3475 _finalizing_box.skeleton(height=420) 

3476 # (DATA-9's ordered source-config group — description · options · data 

3477 # location · column mapping — is now the top of the Data page reserved 

3478 # above. VIZ-31 had already moved "Experimental Setup" out of it: monitor 

3479 # geometry, fonts, text colour and plot background are figure settings, and 

3480 # they render in the Scanpath rail beside the layers they restyle.) 

3481 

3482 # Load + map core data. The **Upload** source renders each table as an 

3483 # [upload box → mapping] group in the sidebar (words, fixations, raw gaze) and 

3484 # normalizes inline; every other source auto-detects (or, for public datasets, 

3485 # renders standalone mapping panels) via prepare_data. Keep the raw frames 

3486 # around so we can show them if the mapping isn't ready. 

3487 # 

3488 # Decide which participant (if any) the OneStop loader should fast-path to. 

3489 # 1. A URL deep link (?participant=) → load just that pid's shard (embedded 

3490 # review use case); captured once so the live selector can't change it. 

3491 # 2. Otherwise, if the full CSV bundle exists → load the whole corpus once 

3492 # (participant=None) and let in-app participant switching just *filter* 

3493 # it — so changing participant is instant instead of re-invoking the 

3494 # loader on every change. 

3495 # 3. Shards-only setup with no full bundle → fall back to lazy per-pid 

3496 # loading driven by the selector (the ~60 GB corpus can't be held whole). 

3497 deeplink_pid = st.session_state.get("_deeplink_participant") 

3498 if deeplink_pid: 

3499 deep_link_pid = deeplink_pid 

3500 elif data_choice == ONESTOP_CHOICE and not onestop_full_bundle_exists(): 

3501 deep_link_pid = st.session_state.get("single_participant") 

3502 elif data_choice == MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE: 

3503 # MultiplEYE has no full-corpus bundle: each session is its own shard, so 

3504 # the live participant selector fast-paths to one session's shards too. 

3505 deep_link_pid = st.session_state.get("single_participant") 

3506 else: 

3507 deep_link_pid = None 

3508 raw_gaze_df: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None 

3509 # Did this load already draw the editable pre-normalization mapping panels 

3510 # into the page's Column mapping section? (Mode A — see the dispatch below.) 

3511 mapping_editor_rendered = False 

3512 # Start each load with a clean column-mapping stash; each branch below 

3513 # records the schema it used for the Data page's mapping section. 

3514 _reset_active_mapping() 

3515 if data_choice == UPLOAD_CHOICE: 

3516 # Hybrid setup wizard: a guided flow on first load, then a compact 

3517 # collapsed "Data & mapping" panel. DATA-26 made it the **Data page's 

3518 # add-a-dataset mode** — adding a dataset *is* setup, and a wizard that 

3519 # lived anywhere else would re-create the two-places-for-one-job problem 

3520 # the page exists to fix. It still owns the page while active: there is 

3521 # nothing for the other views to draw until it finishes, so `main` 

3522 # returns here exactly as before. `_enter_add_data_wizard` requests the 

3523 # Data view when the ➕ button is clicked, so the user is already here. 

3524 wizard_active = not st.session_state.get("setup_complete", False) 

3525 # Imported lazily (not at module top) to avoid the app⇄wizard import cycle. 

3526 from scanpath_studio.wizard import _render_data_setup 

3527 

3528 with setup_wizard_slot: 

3529 setup = _render_data_setup(active=wizard_active) 

3530 words_df, fixations_df = setup.words, setup.fixations 

3531 raw_gaze_df = setup.raw_gaze 

3532 raw_words_df, raw_fixations_df = setup.raw_words, setup.raw_fixations 

3533 mapping_problems = setup.problems 

3534 if wizard_active: 

3535 _render_offpage_setup_notice(data_view) 

3536 return 

3537 elif data_choice == AUTHOR_CHOICE: 

3538 words_df, fixations_df = _render_authoring_source() 

3539 raw_words_df, raw_fixations_df = words_df, fixations_df 

3540 raw_gaze_df = pd.DataFrame() 

3541 mapping_problems = [] 

3542 elif data_choice in st.session_state.get("_datasets", {}): 

3543 # A dataset the user uploaded earlier and named — its frames were 

3544 # normalized once by the wizard and stored in session, so switching back 

3545 # to it is instant (no re-upload, no re-mapping). See _render_data_setup's 

3546 # finalize and render_sidebar_data_source. 

3547 stored = st.session_state["_datasets"][data_choice] 

3548 words_df, fixations_df = stored["words"], stored["fixations"] 

3549 raw_gaze_df = stored["raw_gaze"] 

3550 raw_words_df, raw_fixations_df = words_df, fixations_df 

3551 mapping_problems = [] 

3552 # Re-publish this dataset's chosen filter fields so the sidebar 

3553 # "Filter trials" panel offers the same dynamic conditions. 

3554 st.session_state["wizard_filter_fields"] = list(stored.get("filter_fields", [])) 

3555 # Restore the composite trial-id components (session-only state) so the 

3556 # trial picker renders its Participant/Text cascade — every other load 

3557 # path sets this, but the stored branch doesn't re-normalize. Without it 

3558 # the picker would inherit whatever source was loaded last. 

3559 composite = list(stored.get("composite_trial_columns") or []) 

3560 st.session_state["_composite_trial_columns"] = composite or None 

3561 # Re-publish the stored column mapping so the Data Inspection tab shows 

3562 # how this dataset's columns were mapped (the wizard isn't re-run here). 

3563 for table, schema in (stored.get("schemas") or {}).items(): 

3564 _stash_active_mapping(table, schema) 

3565 else: 

3566 # Built-in sources (demo / synthetic / OneStop / public) auto-detect 

3567 # their mapping, so they skip the wizard entirely. Drop any wizard filter 

3568 # fields left over from a prior upload so the sidebar falls back to the 

3569 # built-in default conditions for these sources. 

3570 st.session_state.pop("wizard_filter_fields", None) 

3571 # Re-propose the column mapping when the monitor-defining source changes. 

3572 # The `col_map_*` widget keys persist across reruns, so a previous corpus' 

3573 # mapping sticks to the next one — e.g. PoTeC maps Trial → `text_id`, and 

3574 # since MultiplEYE *also* has a `text_id` column the stale-column reset 

3575 # (which only fires when a mapped column vanishes) wouldn't catch it, so 

3576 # MultiplEYE's per-page `trial_id` was ignored and every page collapsed 

3577 # into one stimulus-level trial. Clearing on source change lets each 

3578 # corpus auto-detect its own mapping; same-source reruns (and restores) 

3579 # keep their keys. Mirrors the canvas re-seed in render_sidebar_canvas_controls. 

3580 source_key = (data_choice, st.session_state.get("public_dataset_choice")) 

3581 if st.session_state.get("_colmap_seeded_for") != source_key: 

3582 for stale in [ 

3583 k 

3584 for k in list(st.session_state) 

3585 if isinstance(k, str) and k.startswith("col_map_") 

3586 ]: 

3587 del st.session_state[stale] 

3588 st.session_state["_colmap_seeded_for"] = source_key 

3589 raw_words_df, raw_fixations_df = load_words_and_fixations( 

3590 data_choice, 

3591 participant=deep_link_pid, 

3592 # DATA-9 ordered group: a public dataset renders its caption / source 

3593 # options / data-location controls into these reserved sub-slots. 

3594 description_host=description_slot, 

3595 options_host=source_options_slot, 

3596 location_host=data_location_slot, 

3597 ) 

3598 words_df, fixations_df, mapping_problems = prepare_data( 

3599 raw_words_df, 

3600 raw_fixations_df, 

3601 # Show the Column-mapping panels for public datasets AND the Bundled 

3602 # Demo (DATA-8) so the re-mapping capability is discoverable on the 

3603 # default first-load source; pre-filled with auto-detection, so an 

3604 # untouched mapping normalizes identically. 

3605 allow_override=(data_choice in (PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE, DEMO_CHOICE)), 

3606 # Mode A of the Data page's one Column mapping section (DATA-26). 

3607 mapping_host=mapping_body_slot, 

3608 ) 

3609 mapping_editor_rendered = data_choice in (PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE, DEMO_CHOICE) 

3610 if mapping_problems: 

3611 # A required column is still unmapped. Rather than halt the whole app 

3612 # (which hid the data the user needs to choose the mapping), show the 

3613 # raw tables on the Data page, right under the still-editable Column 

3614 # mapping section — and, from any other view, say where that page is. 

3615 with unmapped_slot: 

3616 _render_unmapped_view(raw_words_df, raw_fixations_df, mapping_problems) 

3617 _render_offpage_setup_notice(data_view) 

3618 return 

3619 

3620 # VIZ-14: local/desktop users can attach stimulus screenshots without 

3621 # adding an image_path column to their data. This intentionally stays out 

3622 # of public deployments and share links because it contains machine-local 

3623 # filesystem information; the same resolver is available through the API 

3624 # and CLI for reproducible headless renders. 

3625 if local_filesystem_enabled(): 

3626 with data_location_slot.expander("Stimulus images", expanded=False): 

3627 image_root = st.text_input( 

3628 "Image folder", 

3629 key="stimulus_image_root", 

3630 placeholder="/path/to/stimulus-images", 

3631 help="Local folder containing one image per text or trial.", 

3632 ).strip() 

3633 image_pattern = st.text_input( 

3634 "Filename pattern", 

3635 key="stimulus_image_pattern", 

3636 value="{text_id}.png", 

3637 help="Use table fields such as {text_id}, {trial_id}, or " 

3638 "{participant_id}; subfolders are supported.", 

3639 ).strip()
